protocol-wire-types.title: ApprovalDecision cannot decode the two data-carrying CommandExecution approval variants
protocol-wire-types.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:42-64 `CommandExecutionApprovalDecision` (camelCase) has 6 variants including `AcceptWithExecpolicyAmendment { execpolicy_amendment }` and `ApplyNetworkPolicyAmendment { network_policy_amendment }`; the approval response carries `pub decision: CommandExecutionApprovalDecision` (item.rs:1325-1326).
protocol-wire-types.swiftStatus: Sources/WireProtocol/ServerRequest.swift:4-6 `ApprovalDecision` is a `String`-backed enum with only `accept, acceptForSession, decline, cancel`; `ServerRequest.decodeDecision` (Sources/ProtocolModel/ServerRequest.swift:261-264) decodes `{decision: ApprovalDecision}` strictly. A client reply of `{"decision":{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment":{...}}}` or `{"applyNetworkPolicyAmendment":{...}}` fails to decode and the approval cannot be processed.
protocol-wire-types.description: Upstream lets the user approve a command AND apply an execpolicy/network-policy amendment, sent as an externally-tagged object decision. Swift's decision enum only models the four bare-string decisions, so those two amendment decisions throw on decode.
protocol-wire-types.fixRecommendation: In Sources/WireProtocol/ServerRequest.swift, extend `ApprovalDecision` (or `decodeDecision`) to accept the object forms `{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment": {...}}` and `{"applyNetworkPolicyAmendment": {...}}`, carrying the nested amendment payload (can be `JSONValue` if the amendment types are not otherwise modeled), and map them to accept-with-amendment semantics.

protocol-wire-types.title: Invented `contextMessage` ThreadItem variant has no upstream counterpart
protocol-wire-types.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:209-362 `ThreadItem` (tagged on `type`, camelCase) enumerates exactly 16 variants: userMessage, hookPrompt, agentMessage, plan, reasoning, commandExecution, fileChange, mcpToolCall, dynamicToolCall, collabAgentToolCall, webSearch, imageView, imageGeneration, enteredReviewMode, exitedReviewMode, contextCompaction. protocol-wire-types.description: Swift emits a `contextMessage` item type that is not part of the upstream v2 `ThreadItem` union, so a frontend generated from upstream's TS types treats it as an unknown item. Upstream surfaces initial/developer context inside model history (core context_manager), not as a wire ThreadItem.
protocol-wire-types.fixRecommendation: Either drop the `contextMessage` item from the wire (surface env/developer context via a `userMessage`/developer item or not at all on the v2 surface), or document it as a deliberate, frontend-coordinated port extension. At minimum it should not appear in `item/started`/`item/completed` streams a stock upstream frontend consumes.

protocol-wire-types.title: ClientInfo.version optional in Swift but required upstream
protocol-wire-types.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v1.rs:37-41 `ClientInfo { name: String, title: Option<String>, version: String }` — `version` is a required (non-Option) field.
protocol-wire-types.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/ClientRequest.swift:4-11 `ClientInfo` declares `var version: String?` (optional), so a client omitting `version` is accepted where upstream would reject it.

app-server-registry.title: serverRequest/resolved notification never emitted on server-request resolution
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs:721-744 resolve_pending_server_request() sends ServerNotification::ServerRequestResolved(ServerRequestResolvedNotification { thread_id, request_id }) to all subscribed connections; thread_state.rs:148-178 resolve_server_request_on_thread_listener; bespoke_event_handling.rs:1600,1682,1754,1889,1940 call it from all five server->client response handlers (user-input, MCP elicitation, permissions, file-change approval, command-execution approval). Wire method 'serverRequest/resolved' (common.rs:1492).

The Swift port routes the decision back to the worker but never tells subscribed connections the request was resolved, so a second client viewing the same thread keeps a stale/hung approval prompt.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: In RequestRouter.handle (case .response/.error) — or in SessionSupervisor.deliverServerResponse where the pending thread id is known — after resolving a server request, look up the threadId for that requestId (pendingServerRequests map already holds it) and broadcast Event .serverRequestResolved(threadId, requestId) to all subscribers of that thread. Emit it for all five server-request types on both success and client-error responses (upstream emits unconditionally before processing the response value).

app-server-registry.title: thread/turns/items/list returns real items instead of upstream -32601 stub

app-server-registry.title: Experimental/threadId pre-checks run before params deserialization (message-text divergence in error-overlap cases)
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/message_processor.rs:536-541 deserializes ClientRequest first (invalid params -> invalid_request -32600 'Invalid request: ...'); only then dispatch_initialized_client_request (792-796) checks experimental_reason() -> invalid_request -32600 '<reason> requires experimentalApi capability'.

To match upstream message ordering exactly, parse params first and derive experimental rejection from the typed request (as upstream does via experimental_reason()), reporting deserialization errors before gating. app-server-events.title: thread/status/changed notification is never emitted (entire ThreadWatchManager status machinery missing)
app-server-events.rustEvidence: app-server/src/thread_status.rs:285-339 resolve_thread_status + upsert_thread/remove_thread build ThreadStatusChangedNotification; bespoke_event_handling.rs:152-154 note_turn_started, :184-186 note_turn_completed, :497/526/692/750 acquire WaitingOnApproval/WaitingOnUserInput guards, all routed through ThreadWatchManager which emits ServerNotification::ThreadStatusChanged on every real status transition (active{activeFlags}/idle/systemError/notLoaded).

No active/idle/waitingOnApproval/waitingOnUserInput transitions are ever published from SessionSupervisor, RequestRouter, or SessionEngine.
app-server-events.description: Upstream broadcasts thread/status/changed whenever a thread becomes active (turn start), goes idle (turn complete), enters systemError, or is waiting on an approval/user-input answer. A CodexApp frontend uses this to drive per-thread busy/idle/awaiting-input indicators. The Swift port emits this notification nowhere, so the frontend never receives any status transition.

Only emit when status actually changes (parity with status_changed_notification's previous-vs-current comparison).

app-server-events.title: process/exited omits required stdout/stderr/cap fields; process/outputDelta omits capReached
app-server-events.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/v2/process.rs:165-175 ProcessOutputDeltaNotification requires {processHandle, stream, deltaBase64, capReached}; :181-204 ProcessExitedNotification requires {processHandle, exitCode, stdout, stdoutCapReached, stderr, stderrCapReached} (all non-Option, always serialized).

A strict TS decoder of ProcessExitedNotification would fail on the missing required fields, and a non-streaming client never receives the buffered stdout/stderr.

Mirror the command/exec implementation which already tracks caps correctly.

session-turn-loop.title: turn/steer never produces NoActiveTurn / ExpectedTurnMismatch / EmptyInput errors
session-turn-loop.rustEvidence: app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:661-721 maps SteerInputError into invalid_request (-32600): NoActiveTurn → "no active turn to steer"; ExpectedTurnMismatch → "expected active turn id `X` but found `Y`"; EmptyInput → "input must not be empty". steer_input is given Some(&params.expected_turn_id) (line 657).
session-turn-loop.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1718-1740 only validates empty expectedTurnId and input-too-large, then always replies TurnSteerResponse. The engine handler Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:502 `case .steer(let input, _)` DISCARDS expectedTurnId and unconditionally appends to pendingInput; SessionSupervisor.swift:326-340 submit returns true whenever a worker exists. No NoActiveTurn, ExpectedTurnMismatch, or EmptyInput error is ever produced.
session-turn-loop.description: Upstream turn/steer is a validating RPC: steering with no active turn, with a stale expectedTurnId, or with empty input each returns a JSON-RPC invalid_request error. The Swift accepts every steer unconditionally (buffering input into pendingInput) and replies success, so a frontend that relies on these errors to detect a race (turn already ended, wrong turn id) or to reject empty input gets a false success and silently mis-buffered input. The in-code comment at RequestRouter.swift:1723-1724 asserts the engine produces these errors, but the engine does not.
session-turn-loop.fixRecommendation: In SessionEngine's .steer handler (and/or RequestRouter.turnSteer), check active-turn state: if no current turn → emit/return invalid_request "no active turn to steer"; if currentTurn id != expectedTurnId → "expected active turn id `<expected>` but found `<actual>`"; if input is empty → "input must not be empty". Stop discarding expectedTurnId in EngineOp.steer.

session-turn-loop.title: ActiveTurnNotSteerable error must carry review/compact-specific message and data, only for steer
session-turn-loop.rustEvidence: turn_processor.rs:677-710: ActiveTurnNotSteerable only arises from turn/steer of a Review or Compact active turn, with message "cannot steer a review turn"/"cannot steer a compact turn" and data = serialized TurnError{codex_error_info: ActiveTurnNotSteerable{turn_kind}}. turn/start (turn_processor.rs:329+) does NOT reject an in-progress turn — it submits Op::UserTurn which calls spawn_task → abort_all_tasks(TurnAbortReason::Replaced) (core/src/tasks/mod.rs:308), replacing the active turn.
session-turn-loop.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:538-551 startSpecial REJECTS every new turn (including a regular runTurn) when currentTurn != nil, emitting ActiveTurnNotSteerable with turnKind falling back to .compact for regular turns. There is no replace-on-start path.
session-turn-loop.description: Two divergences: (a) the Swift uses the steer-only ActiveTurnNotSteerable error for a turn/start collision and even fabricates a .compact turnKind for a regular turn; upstream uses this code only for steering review/compact turns. (b) Upstream replaces an active turn on a new turn/start (emitting turn/completed{interrupted} for the replaced turn), whereas the Swift rejects the new submission entirely. A frontend issuing turn/start while a turn is active will see an error instead of the prior turn being interrupted and replaced.
session-turn-loop.fixRecommendation: Route turn/start collisions through an interrupt-then-start (replace) path emitting turn/completed{interrupted, reason Replaced} for the prior turn, matching abort_all_tasks(Replaced). Reserve the ActiveTurnNotSteerable error exclusively for turn/steer of review/compact turns, with the correct per-kind message and data payload.

session-turn-loop.title: Interrupted-turn history marker is not persisted to the rollout
session-turn-loop.rustEvidence: core/src/tasks/mod.rs:854-868 handle_task_abort, on TurnAbortReason::Interrupted, records the marker into history via record_into_history AND persist_rollout_items(&[RolloutItem::ResponseItem(marker)]) then flush_rollout, explicitly before emitting TurnAborted (comment: "Ensure the marker is durably visible before emitting TurnAborted").

The subsequent persist(.turnBoundary, status:.interrupted) writes a boundary record, not the marker ResponseItem. No persist(.item ...) for the abort marker exists.

After a resume/fork the model history reconstructed from the rollout will be missing the interrupted-turn marker that upstream guarantees is durably present, so a resumed thread loses the 'previous turn was interrupted' guidance and diverges from upstream history.
session-turn-loop.fixRecommendation: In finishTurn, when status == .interrupted, also persist the abort marker as a rollout ResponseItem (e.g. persist(.item(turnId:, item: the contextMessage)) ) and ensure the durability barrier/flush runs before emitting turn/completed, mirroring tasks/mod.rs:859-867.

session-turn-loop.title: Diff tracker emits a redundant turn/diff/updated for an exact-empty delta

Low traffic and cosmetic on the client, but a strict diff-event stream comparison will diverge.

session-turn-loop.title: Goal runtime auto-continuation / budget-limited abort not reproduced
session-turn-loop.rustEvidence: core/src/goals.rs:383-394 GoalRuntimeEvent::MaybeContinueIfIdle → maybe_continue_goal_if_idle_runtime (auto-starts another turn when the goal is incomplete and the session is idle); TaskAborted handling and BudgetLimited abort reason (protocol.rs:3711) are driven through goal_runtime_apply at tasks/mod.rs:342,510-519,761-769,802-807.

session-turn-loop.description: Upstream's goal runtime can autonomously continue a thread (start a new turn when idle and the goal is unmet) and abort a turn when the goal budget is exhausted. The Swift only injects goal text and tracks usage/budget, so a thread driven by an active goal will not auto-continue or self-terminate on budget the way upstream does. This is the experimental goals feature; affects only goal-driven threads.

context-compaction.title: Encrypted reasoning/compaction items are token-estimated by full-JSON byte count instead of upstream estimate_reasoning_length()
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/context_manager/history.rs:499-510,534-545 — estimate_item_token_count → estimate_response_item_model_visible_bytes special-cases Reasoning{encrypted_content:Some}, Compaction, and ContextCompaction{encrypted_content:Some} to `estimate_reasoning_length(content.len())` = `len*3/4 - 650` (saturating), NOT the serialized JSON size. This feeds get_total_token_usage (history.rs:309-327) and estimate_token_count_with_base_instructions (history.rs:144-158).
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/ContextManager.swift:38-43 — modelVisibleBytes always returns `JSONEncoder().encode(item).count`; estimateItemTokens = ceil(bytes/4) for every item including `.reasoning(...,encryptedContent:)` and `.contextCompaction`. Comment at lines 38-40 asserts 'no encrypted reasoning... cases', but appendReasoning (line 166-171) stores encryptedContent and it is serialized into the estimate. No `estimate_reasoning_length` / `*3/4-650` logic exists.
context-compaction.description: Upstream costs an encrypted reasoning (or compaction) item as roughly the decoded payload size in tokens minus 650, because the server already accounted for those tokens and the base64 blob is not what the model re-ingests as text. Swift instead counts ceil(serialized_base64_json_bytes/4), which for a typical multi-KB encrypted reasoning blob over-counts by a large factor. Because get_total_token_usage / totalTokenUsage drives the auto-compact threshold and recompute_token_usage drives the post-compaction token gauge (thread/tokenUsage/updated), the divergence causes compaction to trigger at the wrong point and reports a different token total to the frontend than upstream would.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: In ContextManager.swift add a Reasoning/Compaction special case in estimateItemTokens: when the item carries encryptedContent, return max(0, encryptedContent.utf8.count * 3 / 4 - 650) (port of estimate_reasoning_length) instead of JSON byte count; otherwise keep the JSON-byte path. Apply the same to `.contextCompaction` if it can carry encrypted content.

context-compaction.title: Post-compaction "Heads up" WarningEvent is emitted on the remote-compaction path in Swift but not upstream
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/compact.rs:290-293 emits the WarningEvent('Heads up: Long threads and multiple compactions...') only at the end of run_compact_task_inner_impl (LOCAL compaction). core/src/compact_remote.rs and compact_remote_v2.rs contain no WarningEvent emission (grep confirmed empty).
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1725 emits `.warning(... Compaction.headsUpWarning)` inside installCompactedHistory, which is the shared tail for BOTH the local path and the remote path (tryRemoteCompaction → installCompactedHistory at lines 1434-1451).
context-compaction.description: Upstream only warns the user after local (model-streamed) compaction; remote `/responses/compact` compaction completes silently. Swift routes both through installCompactedHistory and always emits the warning, so a frontend driven by the Swift server sees an extra WarningNotification after remote compactions that upstream never sends.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Move the `emit(.warning(... headsUpWarning))` call out of the shared installCompactedHistory and into the local-only branch (after the streamLoop completes, before installCompactedHistory), or pass a flag into installCompactedHistory indicating local-vs-remote and gate the warning on local.

context-compaction.title: Remote-compaction request failure falls back to local compaction in Swift; upstream treats it as terminal
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/compact_remote.rs:128-135 — on Err from run_remote_compact_task_inner_impl, upstream sends EventMsg::Error('Error running remote compact task') and returns Err(err); run_auto_compact (session/turn.rs:836-843) propagates it. There is no remote→local fallback: provider support is decided up-front by should_use_remote_compact_task and a supported-provider remote failure fails the compact task.
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1600-1611 — tryRemoteCompaction catches any error from model.compactConversationHistory, writes to stderr, and returns nil; runCompactionFlow then proceeds to the local streaming path (lines 1454+). Both 'provider unsupported' and 'remote errored' map to the same nil fallback.
context-compaction.description: When a provider that supports remote compaction has the remote request fail, upstream surfaces an Error event and aborts the compaction (and turn); Swift silently re-runs compaction locally. The 'provider unsupported → local' part is correct, but the 'remote errored → local fallback' part diverges from upstream's terminal semantics, changing the error/Event surface a frontend observes on remote-compaction failure.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Distinguish 'unsupported provider' (return nil → local) from 'remote request errored' (surface an Error event mirroring upstream's 'Error running remote compact task' and fail the compaction) in tryRemoteCompaction, rather than collapsing both into a local fallback.

context-compaction.title: Swift-only maxCompactionsPerTurn backstop can fail a turn upstream's uncapped mid-turn loop would continue
context-compaction.rustEvidence: core/src/session/turn.rs:497-517 — the mid-turn auto-compact branch is explicitly uncapped: the comment states 'as long as compaction works well in getting us way below the token limit, we shouldn't worry about being in an infinite loop'; it simply `continue`s after each run_auto_compact with no per-turn compaction counter.
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:2459-2465 increments `compactions` and, when `compactions > limits.maxCompactionsPerTurn` (Sources/InfraPrimitives/Limits.swift:38, default 4), sets status=.failed with ErrorBody(codexErrorInfo:'LoopGuard') and breaks the sampling loop.
context-compaction.description: Swift adds a hard cap (default 4) on compactions per turn that upstream does not have. A pathological long turn that legitimately needs more than 4 mid-turn compactions terminates with a LoopGuard error in Swift, whereas upstream keeps compacting and continuing. This is a defensive backstop but is an observable behavioral divergence (a turn-failure that upstream would not produce).
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Either raise the default to a value high enough to be unreachable in normal operation (matching upstream's effectively-unbounded behavior) or gate the LoopGuard on a separate no-progress condition (e.g. compaction failed to reduce tokens below the limit) rather than a fixed count, to mirror upstream's 'compaction gets us below the limit' assumption.

The Swift string-interpolation of the error enum also leaks Swift Debug syntax (malformed("...")).
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Thread a line counter through parseInternal/parseChunk and reconstruct the upstream Display: prefix InvalidPatch-class messages with "invalid patch: " and hunk-class messages with "invalid hunk at line N, "; and at the call sites (ToolRouter.swift:555, RemoteExecServerTools.swift:1023) emit the human-readable message (not String(describing:) of the enum) under the prefix "apply_patch verification failed: " to match handlers/apply_patch.rs.

persistence-rollout.title: archive() flips a DB flag but does not move the rollout file into archived_sessions/
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: thread-store/src/local/archive_thread.rs:41-59: archive_thread creates `<codex_home>/archived_sessions/`, std::fs::rename()s the canonical rollout file from `sessions/` into it, then calls state-db mark_archived(thread_id, archived_path, now). rollout/src/recorder.rs:1159-1174 list_archived_threads scans the `archived_sessions` subdir on disk; rollout/src/metadata.rs:213-272 backfill treats files found under ARCHIVED_SESSIONS_SUBDIR as archived. persistence-rollout.description: Upstream archiving moves the rollout JSONL from sessions/ to archived_sessions/ and records archived_at, so directory-scanning consumers (list_archived_threads, backfill) and any cross-tool reader see the thread as archived. The Swift port keeps the file in the active sessions/ tree and only sets a DB flag, so a directory scan (upstream or any tool not sharing the Swift SQLite DB) still classifies the thread as active, and the recorded location is inconsistent with upstream's location-based archive semantics.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: In ThreadStore.archive(), after quiescing/closing the writer, move the resolved rollout file to `<codexHome>/archived_sessions/<basename>` (mkdir -p first), update the DB row's rollout_path and an archived_at timestamp, and have unarchive() move it back to the sessions/ date-partitioned tree. persistence-rollout.title: Compacted sidecar emits context_compacted but no equivalent of ThreadRolledBack rollback markers / replacement-history-driven reverse replay nuances
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: protocol.rs:1303 EventMsg::ContextCompacted(ContextCompactedEvent) is a fieldless `{"type":"context_compacted"}`; protocol.rs:1306,3178-3182 EventMsg::ThreadRolledBack(ThreadRolledBackEvent{num_turns:u32}) is the durable marker that rollout_reconstruction.rs:130-133,274-276 and thread_rollout_truncation.rs:46-50,80-96 consume to drop the last N user turns during replay.
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Rollout.swift:474-483 emits the correct fieldless `context_compacted` sidecar (good). But ThreadStore.rollback() (ThreadStore.swift:459-509) physically rewrites the rollout file dropping the last N turn groups (rewriteRollout) and never writes a `thread_rolled_back` event_msg marker; the Swift reader has no case for `thread_rolled_back`.
persistence-rollout.description: Upstream represents rollback as an in-stream ThreadRolledBack marker that reverse-replay and truncation interpret, preserving the full forward history with a logical rollback. The Swift port instead destructively truncates the file. For codex-swift's own self-consistent replay this is acceptable, but an upstream reader of a thread that was rolled back via codex-swift would see a permanently shortened history with no rollback provenance, and codex-swift cannot interpret a `thread_rolled_back` marker written by upstream (it would be dropped as an unknown event_msg).
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: Lower priority: if cross-tool rollback fidelity is desired, append a `{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"thread_rolled_back","num_turns":N}}` line instead of (or in addition to) rewriting the file, and add a `thread_rolled_back` case to RolloutReader.rustEventRecords that drops the last N user turns on replay.

config.title: Config write path performs no ConfigToml schema/type validation

config.description: Upstream rejects writes that would make the merged user config fail `ConfigToml` deserialization (wrong scalar type, invalid enum variant) with `configValidationError`; Swift silently accepts and persists any well-formed TOML value, so a client can write a config that upstream would refuse and that may break later loads.
config.fixRecommendation: After applying edits in handleConfigWriteRequest, validate the resulting root (and the effective merged config) against the known ConfigToml field types/enum variants; on failure return WireError.configWriteError(code: "configValidationError", ...). config.title: Write `version` computed over transformed user layer, not raw config.toml; breaks expected_version round-trip

config.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:5970-5974 userLayerVersion() computes ConfigCanonicalVersion.version over the `"toml"` layer's values, which have `profiles` stripped and the inline profile overlay merged in (Config.swift:822-838). But readUserConfigTOML/persistTOML (RequestRouter.swift:6032, 5908) operate on the RAW file with profiles intact.
config.description: The `version` reported by config write (and compared for `expectedVersion`) is computed over a profiles-stripped, overlay-applied transform of the user config, while the file actually read/written is the raw file. Whenever a `[profiles]` table or active inline profile exists, the reported version is not the version of the on-disk file, so a read→write optimistic-concurrency round-trip can spuriously conflict or fail to detect real conflicts.
config.fixRecommendation: Compute userLayerVersion over the RAW config.toml content (readUserConfigTOML(path)) using ConfigCanonicalVersion.version, matching the bytes actually persisted, rather than over the stripped/overlaid `"toml"` layer.

mcp.title: OAuth login redirect URI and client_id diverge from upstream dynamic ephemeral-port flow
mcp.rustEvidence: codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/perform_oauth_login.rs:370-394 local_redirect_uri builds `http://{ip}:{port}/callback` against an ephemeral-bound loopback port, with a per-server callback-id appended to the path (append_callback_id_to_redirect_uri, callback_id_from_server_url SHA256→base64url at :396-419); client_id comes from dynamic registration / config oauth.client_id, not a fixed literal.

mcp.description: The Swift MCP OAuth login is a separate simplified implementation: fixed loopback port 1455 and a static `/mcp/oauth/callback` path with no per-server callback-id, plus a hardcoded `client_id=Codex`. mcp.fixRecommendation: If OAuth MCP login parity is required, reimplement the redirect URI to bind an ephemeral loopback port and append the per-server callback-id (SHA256 of the normalized server URL, base64url no-pad, first 9 bytes), and source client_id from config (oauth.client_id) / dynamic client registration rather than the literal "Codex"; honor mcp_oauth_callback_port / mcp_oauth_callback_url overrides.

hooks.title: Exit-code 2 for PostToolUse incorrectly blocks instead of injecting feedback
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/events/post_tool_use.rs:256-269 — `Some(2) => { if let Some(reason)=trimmed_non_empty(stderr) { entries.push(Feedback); feedback_messages_for_model.push(reason); } else { status=Failed } }`. PostToolUse exit-2 stderr is FEEDBACK (additional model context), it does NOT block — the tool already ran.
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:1396-1428 — the generic exit-2 path returns `HookOutcome(decision: .block, reason: txt)` for every non-Stop event, including .postToolUse. This turns PostToolUse exit-2 into a block.
hooks.description: Upstream treats PostToolUse exit-code 2 with stderr as model feedback (no block); Swift treats it as decision:block. For PostToolUse a block is semantically wrong (the tool output already exists) and would surface a spurious blockingReason.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In Hooks.swift runCommand(), branch the exit-2 handling per req.eventName. For .postToolUse: return decision .allow with the stderr text carried as additionalContext (feedback), not as a block.

hooks.title: Exit-code 2 for SessionStart incorrectly blocks instead of failing

hooks.fixRecommendation: In runCommand(), for .sessionStart treat any non-zero exit (including 2) as a Failed/allow outcome with no block; only exit 0 + non-JSON stdout becomes additionalContext.

hooks.title: Exit-code 2 for PreCompact/PostCompact incorrectly aborts compaction
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/events/compact.rs:275-282 — both PreCompact and PostCompact have NO `Some(2)` arm; exit 2 → `Some(code) => { status=Failed; text = stderr or "hook exited with code {code}" }`. Compact hooks abort only via stdout `continue:false`, never via exit 2.

hooks.description: A PreCompact/PostCompact hook exiting with code 2 will be treated by Swift as decision:block and abort the compaction, whereas upstream just records a Failed hook run and proceeds with compaction.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In runCommand(), exclude .preCompact/.postCompact from the generic exit-2 block path; treat their exit 2 as a Failed/allow outcome (surface via outputSchemaError if a failed signal is wanted).

hooks.title: Trust-state key index math diverges for grouped / multi-handler hooks.json
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/lib.rs:91-101 hook_key = `{key_source}:{event_key_label}:{group_index}:{handler_index}`; discovery.rs:418-472 — group_index is `enumerate()` over the matcher-groups *within one event*, handler_index is `enumerate()` over the command handlers *within that group*. event_key_label is snake_case (lib.rs:77-88).
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:492-514 — key = `"\(path):\(eventName):\(index):0"` where `index` is the flattened `rawHooks.enumerated()` index across ALL hooks in the file and handler_index is hard-coded `0`.
hooks.description: For any hooks.json in the canonical grouped-object form with more than one group per event, more than one handler per group, or more than one event, Swift's running `index` (used as group_index) and constant `0` handler_index will not match upstream's per-event group_index/handler_index. The trust key therefore won't match the persisted `[hooks.state.<key>]` written by the Rust client, so the hook fails its trusted_hash check and never runs (or, conversely, an attacker-modified hook could collide a different key). The trust gate is the core security mechanism.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In load()/parse(), when flattening the grouped form, carry the true (group_index, handler_index) from the nested structure and build the key as `"\(path):\(snakeEvent):\(groupIndex):\(handlerIndex)"`; for the flat-array legacy form, derive group/handler indices the way the loader that wrote the state did, rather than a single running counter with handler_index 0.

hooks.title: Malformed-JSON hook stdout silently no-ops instead of marking the run Failed
hooks.rustEvidence: Every event parse_completed: e.g. pre_tool_use.rs:241-247, post_tool_use.rs:248-254, stop.rs:195-201, session_start.rs:193-199 — when exit 0 and `looks_like_json(stdout)` (starts with `{` or `[`) but parse fails, status=Failed with an "hook returned invalid <event> JSON output" Error entry.
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:1275-1445 — JSON path requires `trimmed.hasPrefix("{")` AND successful JSONSerialization. If it fails (or stdout starts with `[`), control falls through; exit-2 check is skipped (exit 0), the bare-text path is gated out by the `{`/`[` prefix, and runCommand returns `HookOutcome(decision:.allow)` with no outputSchemaError. summarize() then reports status `completed`, not `failed`.
hooks.description: Invalid JSON output (or any `[`-prefixed JSON) is silently ignored by Swift and reported as a completed hook run; upstream reports a Failed run with an Error entry surfaced on hook/completed. Behavior (no block) is the same, but the HookRunSummary status/entries shown to the frontend diverge.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In runCommand(), when exit==0 and stdout starts with `{`/`[` but JSON parse fails, return an outcome with outputSchemaError set to the upstream message (`hook returned invalid <event> JSON output`) so summarize() emits status `failed` with an error entry.

hooks.title: Generic exit-2 fallback reason text differs from upstream per-event Failed messages
hooks.rustEvidence: Per-event empty-stderr exit-2 messages: pre_tool_use.rs:262 "PreToolUse hook exited with code 2 but did not write a blocking reason to stderr"; post_tool_use.rs:267 "...did not write feedback to stderr"; permission_request.rs:255 "...did not write a denial reason to stderr". hooks.fixRecommendation: Add per-event exit-2 empty-output messages and a generic `hook exited with code {N}` outputSchemaError for nonzero exits other than the event's handled cases, matching the upstream strings, so hook/completed entries carry the same text.

auth.fixRecommendation: In accountJSON, require only email; default planType to "unknown" when the claim is absent: `let planType = claims?.planType ?? "unknown"`.

auth.title: Device-code login start failure mapped to invalid_request instead of internal_error
auth.rustEvidence: account_processor.rs:344-351 login_chatgpt_device_code_start_error: NotFound IoError -> invalid_request(err); any other error -> internal_error("failed to request device code: {err}").

Swift collapses all device-code start failures to invalid_request, so the JSON-RPC error code and message differ for non-NotFound failures.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: UnlessTrusted known-safe short-circuit ignores used_complex_parsing
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/exec_policy.rs:662-668 — `if is_known_safe && !used_complex_parsing && (approval_policy == UnlessTrusted || environment_lacks_sandbox_protections) { return Decision::Allow; }`. `used_complex_parsing` is set true at exec_policy.rs:797-803 when only `parse_shell_lc_single_command_prefix` (not plain decomposition) can decompose the command, suppressing the auto-allow so the user is prompted.
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/ExecPolicy.swift:569-572 — `let isKnownSafe = CommandSafety.classify(argv: argv) == .safe; if isKnownSafe, approvalPolicy.kind == .unlessTrusted { return .safe }`. There is no `used_complex_parsing` flag and no `parse_shell_lc_single_command_prefix` equivalent (grep for usedComplexParsing/single_command_prefix returns nothing), so a known-safe command extracted via complex parsing is auto-allowed under UnlessTrusted instead of prompting.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream forces a prompt for a known-safe command under UnlessTrusted when the command had to be decomposed via the complex single-command-prefix path (e.g. a `bash -lc` script containing redirection/subshells where only a leading `cd ... &&` prefix could be safely extracted). Swift always short-circuits to .safe for any known-safe argv under UnlessTrusted, slightly widening auto-approval in this narrow case.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: In ExecPolicy.swift, thread a `usedComplexParsing` flag through `classify`/`classifyExact` (set true on the single-command-prefix decomposition path, which also needs to be added) and gate the UnlessTrusted known-safe short-circuit on `!usedComplexParsing`, matching exec_policy.rs:662-668.

sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/network_policy_decision.rs:46-72 (`denied_network_policy_message`) maps blocked.reason to detail strings: 'denied' -> 'domain is explicitly denied by policy and cannot be approved from this prompt', 'not_allowed' -> 'domain is not on the allowlist for the current sandbox mode', 'not_allowed_local', 'method_not_allowed', 'proxy_disabled', default -> 'request is blocked by network policy', formatted as `Network access to "{host}" was blocked: {detail}.` (and `Network access was blocked by policy.` when host empty).
